title: Ember and Wolf
premise: Jude Villalobos poisons themselves slowly for a living, tasting the crown's food while secretly keeping ledgers for the Ember Guild, which smuggles gifted people—those who can kindle impossible things—out of the capital. When the new usurper declares a hunt on the gifted, Jude's double life collapses: the ledgers name everyone, and the crown's wolf-hunters are led by the one person Jude ever loved, Serah Vane. Fleeing with the ledgers and a gifted child whose power could reignite the ancient war between ember and crown, Jude must choose between delivering the records to save the free cities or burning them to save the people named inside. In the end, Jude trades their own hard-won immunity—drinking the poison meant for the child's execution—to expose the usurper's crimes at the peace table, and the free cities shelter the gifted under a new law written in Jude's name.
about_author: Coral Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters and swears the best stories were in the evidence boxes. They write fantasy about people whose loyalties don't fit in official ledgers, and they still taste every meal twice.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A routine morning: tasting the usurper's breakfast, cataloguing a shipment of impossible things for the Ember Guild, hiding both lives in one body. When a dish nearly kills Jude and heals too fast, a wolf-hunter notices. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a person whose survival depends on remaining unremarkable.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, with an interlude from guildmaster Ovid. Jude balances the guild's books as the crown announces the Gift Hunt; Ovid orders the ledgers moved to the free cities. Jude discovers a name in the records they never expected: Serah Vane, their first love, now a wolf-hunter. Emotional beat: the past arriving with teeth.

chapters.title: What the Wolf-Hunter Keeps
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah hunts a gifted smuggler through the capital's rooftops and lets her escape, falsifying her report. Flashbacks reveal her history with Jude and why she serves a crown she despises. She is ordered to investigate the Ember Guild. Emotional beat: duty as a cage built from love.

chapters.title: The Child Who Kindled
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The guild's safehouse is raided; Jude escapes with Wren, an eight-year-old whose gift can wake dormant ember-magic in armies of people—an ancient war's spark. Ovid is captured. Jude must choose: run with the ledgers or trade them for Ovid. Emotional beat: terror and fierce, unexpected protectiveness.

chapters.title: Road of Salt and Ash
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Wren's POV. On the road to the free cities, Wren's uncontrolled gift burns a checkpoint, drawing Serah's pursuit. Jude teaches Wren to hold the fire in, and in teaching, admits their own buried gift: they taste truth in every dish. Emotional beat: found family forming under pursuit.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Table
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah presents her findings and is ordered to execute captured guild members publicly, Ovid among them. She recognizes Jude in the crowd of the condemned and realizes the ledgers—and the child—are the usurper's true prize. Emotional beat: the moment loyalty cracks and cannot be mended.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Iron
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude offers the usurper's spymaster the ledgers in exchange for Ovid and Wren's freedom, hiding that Wren travels with them. Serah intercepts the handoff—and instead of arresting Jude, burns her own orders and defects. Emotional beat: love chosen openly against duty at last.

chapters.title: The Hunt Turns
chapters.summary: Serah and Jude's POV, alternating. Hunted together now, they reach the free cities only to find the council willing to trade Wren to the usurper for peace. Jude's ledger proves the usurper poisoned the old king—the very crime Jude tasted and stayed silent about. Emotional beat: guilt made public, justice demanded outside the law.

chapters.title: Ember and Wolf
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. At the peace parley, the usurper demands Wren; when refused, his armies advance and he orders Wren's execution by poison cup. Jude drinks it first, their trained immunity buying time as Serah turns her hunters against their master and Wren's gift wakes—not armies, but the truth, projected for all to see. Emotional beat: sacrifice as testimony.

chapters.title: A Law Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, recovering. The usurper falls to his own council; the free cities pass the Accord, sheltering the gifted. Jude survives the poison, diminished but alive, and opens a new ledger—not of smuggled people, but of returned names. Serah stays. Wren learns to read. Emotional beat: belonging, finally, without hiding.
